peers.name: architect
peers.purpose: Ask about the design when the ticket does not settle it.

commands:
/var/folders/4g/s95glx9x6n71bq4hc08ly2gm0000gn/T/m2-await-wj3POH/bin/wf send architect --await-reply <<'WF_MSG'
Please decide whether retries for charge() in src/payments.ts belong in the client or the queue. The user explicitly reserves this decision for you. Currently charge creates HttpClient on every call, posts /charges with {customer,cents}, throws on status >=500, and returns response.body.id. Please specify retry location and any required policy/idempotency constraints so I can write a short plan without choosing the architecture.
WF_MSG
turns.final: Awaiting the architect’s decision on client versus queue retries.

calls.text: Please decide whether retries for charge() in src/payments.ts belong in the client or the queue. The user explicitly reserves this decision for you. Currently charge creates HttpClient on every call, posts /charges with {customer,cents}, throws on status >=500, and returns response.body.id. Please specify retry location and any required policy/idempotency constraints so I can write a short plan without choosing the architecture.

turns.final: Submitted the plan: queue-owned retries, preserving single-attempt behavior for the shared client and batch path.

calls.result: {"decision":"queue","plan":"Keep charge() and the shared HTTP client single-attempt so the batch path never retries. Add bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter to the queue worker for retryable charge failures; leave permanent failures terminal. Before enabling retries, ensure a stable per-charge idempotency key is reused across attempts to prevent duplicate charges. Test transient recovery, retry exhaustion, permanent failures, idempotency reuse, and that the batch path still makes only one attempt."}
